text:
maya: Heads up — ACME-prod reports embeddings throughput cratered around 2026-03-14T03:20Z. Tokens/sec steady but vectors/sec fell ~115k/s -> ~20k/s. p95 latency on /v1/embeddings shot up from ~18ms to ~420ms.

jordan: Any HTTP errors or timeouts observed, or just slow successful responses? Any infra deploys at that time?

maya: No 5xx. All requests return 200 but slower. ACME said they rolled a client change around the time it started.

sergio: Need sample request + trace id + model chosen by routing to debug.

maya: TraceID trace-9e8f7a6b. Sample (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer ***
X-Embed-Dim: 1536
Content-Type: application/json
{ \"input\": [\"a\",\"b\"], \"model\": \"rwinf-embed-1024-v1\" }
```
Routing picked rwinf-embed-1024-fp16.

maya: Gateway excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-14T03:20:11Z] trace-trace-9e8f7a6b selected_variant=rwinf-embed-1024-fp16 backend=embed-pool-3
[2026-03-14T03:20:11Z] trace-trace-9e8f7a6b header.X-Embed-Dim=1536
[2026-03-14T03:20:12Z] trace-trace-9e8f7a6b model_exec: dim_mismatch -> routed_cpu_fallback=true
[2026-03-14T03:20:12Z] trace-trace-9e8f7a6b enqueue=1.1ms queue_depth=7
[2026-03-14T03:20:12Z] trace-trace-9e8f7a6b exec_gpu=6.0ms exec_cpu=390ms
```

anika: This looks like a vector-dimension mismatch. Client stub is advertising 1536 but model outputs 1024. Our batching key includes vector_dim; mismatch causes requests to fall back to a CPU-safe code path to avoid corrupting GPU memory layout. CPU path is much slower and defeats batching, causing head-of-line blocking and lower aggregate vectors/sec even with high GPU util.

sergio: Confirmed: batching groups by (variant, seq_len, vec_dim). Unexpected vec_dim creates a separate batch key; CPU fallback takes a slot and serializes work.

maya: Repro I ran against prod API:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\
  -H \"X-Embed-Dim: 1536\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{"input": ["hello","world"], "model":"rwinf-embed-1024-v1"}'
```
Response 200 but p95 ~400ms and vectors/sec for tenant drops.

jordan: ACME worried about increased billing from higher CPU and longer request durations. Any quick mitigation we can ask them to do client-side?

anika: Short term: ask client to stop sending X-Embed-Dim header (or set it to correct 1024). We pushed an edge gate that rejects requests where X-Embed-Dim != model_dim with HTTP 422 and an explanatory message — that prevents bad requests from entering GPU queues.

sergio: Medium term runtime fixes: validate shape header in gateway and reject before enqueue, add per-shape batching metrics, and instrument cpu_fallback_rate alerts. Possibly add a fast-path shim that rejects mismatched header without consuming a GPU token.

maya: ACME accepted the 422 gating change and rolled back their client build. After gating, vectors/sec recovered to ~112k/s within ~10 minutes. We cleared the queue and p95 returned to normal.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-432 created and assigned to eng-ml for root-cause and follow-ups.

anika: Follow-ups we've put in the queue: [1] hotfix to validate/reject mismatch at edge (done), [2] dashboard tile showing per-shape batch sizes and cpu_fallback_rate, [3] alert if cpu_fallback_rate > 0.5% for 5m, [4] postmortem and customer note about billing blip.

jordan: I'll draft a short customer-facing timeline + action items: avoid header, confirm client pinned to released SDK.

maya: Summary: throughput regression tracked to malformed X-Embed-Dim header from client -> CPU fallback + batching fragmentation -> head-of-line blocking. Hotfix and customer rollback resolved it. :thumbsup:
